outline.chapter_title: 1. Introduction to Tabular Learning and LLMs
outline.description: Prepares readers for the intersection of tabular data problems with large language models, highlighting key challenges and motivating the need for a new approach.
subtopics: Overview of tabular data characteristics
Role of LLMs in few-shot learning
Limitations of existing LLM-based tabular methods (end-to-end inference, fine-tuning, prompt size)
Problem statement: feature engineering with LLMs
Contribution of FeatLLM: rule extraction, low-cost inference
outline.},{: 2. Foundations of Few-Shot and Transfer Learning in Tabular Domains
outline.description: Provides necessary background on few-shot learning concepts as applied to structured data, and surveys prior transfer‑learning techniques that inspire FeatLLM.
subtopics: Definition and significance of few-shot learning
Spurious correlation problem in low-data regimes
Unsupervised pretraining methods (masking, contrastive)
Transfer learning across diverse tabular datasets (TransTab, TabPFN)
Limitations that motivate rule-based feature synthesis
outline.},{: 3. Language‑Interfaced Tabular Modeling: From Prompting to Inference
outline.description: Explains how LLMs have traditionally been used for tabular prediction, laying the groundwork for FeatLLM’s novel strategy.
subtopics: Serializing tabular data into natural language
In-context learning vs. parameter‑efficient fine‑tuning (LoRA/IA3)
Challenges of large feature sets & long prompts
Existing baseline pipelines (In‑Context, TABLET, TabLLM)
outline.description: Presents a high‑level architecture diagram and clarifies the main components—rule extraction, parsing, weighting, ensemble—and how they interact.
subtopics: Problem formulation (dataset, features, classes)
Key components: prompt design, rule generation, feature bagging, linear weighting, ensemble averaging
Comparison with end‑to‑end LLM pipelines
outline.description: Dives deep into the tripartite prompt structure that guides the LLM to produce interpretable rules while avoiding noise.
subtopics: Basic information description – task framing and feature metadata
Reasoning instruction – two‑step causal inference + demonstration grounding
Response instruction – formatting guidelines for rules and class headers
Managing prompt length via bagging and temperature control
outline.},{: 6. Parsing Natural Language Rules into Programmatic Features
outline.description: Explains how generated rules are translated into executable Python snippets that produce binary feature vectors.
subtopics: Handling syntactic variability in LLM output (phrase changes like "greater than")
LLM as code generator: function scaffolding and execution via exec()
Validation steps to ensure correct rule semantics
Error handling and robustness considerations
outline.},{: 7. Feature Weight Learning and Probability Estimation
outline.description: Describes the lightweight downstream model that learns importance weights for each rule-derived binary feature.
subtopics: Linear model sans bias; weight non‑negativity constraint (ReLU-like)
Equation 1–3 defining logits and softmax probabilities
Cross‑entropy training with few shots
Interpretation of learned weights as rule relevance
outline.},{: 8. Ensemble through Bagging for Robustness and Prompt Scalability
outline.description: Details how multiple random trials reduce spurious rule effects and mitigate prompt size limits.
subtopics: Sampling filters: bag up features or instances per trial
High temperature sampling for diverse rules
Rule diversity analysis & self‑consistency property
Aggregating predictions via average softmax outputs
outline.description: Provides concrete implementation insights on API usage, hyper‑parameters, training loops, and reproducibility notes.
subtopics: API parameters (temperature=0.5 top_p=1)
Number of ensembles=20; rules per class=10
Optimizers (Adam lr=0.01), epochs,& k‑fold CV
Hardware requirements & parallelization options
Reproducibility checklist
